title: High Throughput Processing of Wastewater for SARS-CoV-2 RNA Analysis
author: Aaron Topol
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b2kmqcu6
materials: Briefly centrifuge the conicals for 00:05:00 at 5250 x g, °C, to pull down the bubbles generated during homogenization. Sample is ready for RNA extraction using the Chemagic 360 (see accompanying protocol, extraction may also be done using Kingfisher or several manual Qiagen kits. See protocol for details) . A modification of this step may provide greater sensitivity. The modification entails centrifuging at a higher speed of 24000 x g, °C, to pellet the solids and then extracting the RNA from the resultant supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare samples and equipment
steps.instruction: Keep fresh samples at 4 °C; if frozen, thaw at room temperature. Set centrifuge temperature to 4 °C and oven temperature to 110 °C. Retrieve an aliquot of BCoV from the freezer and thaw on ice.

substeps.instruction: Store fresh samples at 4 °C; thaw frozen samples at room temperature.
Remove BCoV aliquot from freezer and thaw on ice.

steps.title: Label conical tubes
steps.instruction: Label each 50 mL conical with the corresponding sample name.

steps.title: Mix sludge sample
steps.instruction: Invert the sludge sample bottle a few times to mix.

steps.title: Transfer sludge to conicals
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, pour 50 mL of well‑mixed primary sludge into the labeled 50 mL conical; if the sample volume is less than 50 mL, add nuclease‑free water to bring the total to 50 mL.

substeps.instruction: Pour 50 mL well‑mixed sludge into labeled conical.
If volume <50 mL, add nuclease‑free water to reach 50 mL.

steps.title: Arrange rotor for balance
steps.instruction: Bring the rotor into the biosafety cabinet and arrange the conicals so the rotor is balanced.

steps.title: Centrifuge samples
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the samples at 24 000 × g, 4 °C for at least 30 minutes; set the centrifuge time to “Hold”.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant
steps.instruction: In the biosafety cabinet, aspirate the supernatant into a liquid biohazard waste container.

steps.title: Label new conicals and weigh
steps.instruction: Apply a label to a new 50 mL conical for each sample and record the empty conical mass in grams.

substeps.instruction: Weigh empty conical and record mass (g).

steps.title: Transfer pellet aliquot
steps.instruction: Using a plastic or metal spatula, scoop ~0.75 g of dewatered pellet into the pre‑weighed conical, record its mass, and set the remaining pellet aside for dry‑weight measurement.

substeps.instruction: Set remainder aside for later dry‑weight measurement.

steps.title: Prepare BCoV‑DNA/RNA shield stock
steps.instruction: In a new 150 mL bottle, add 1.5 µL rehydrated BCoV vaccine per 1 mL DNA/RNA Shield, mix by inverting or gentle shaking; the resulting solution contains ~5 × 10⁵ BCoV copies / mL. Record catalog numbers: DNA/RNA Shield (Zymo Research #R1100‑50) and BCoV (Zoetis #CALF‑GUARD).

substeps.instruction: Add 1.5 µL rehydrated BCoV per 1 mL DNA/RNA Shield.
Mix by inversion or gentle shaking.

steps.title: Resuspend solids in spiked shield
steps.instruction: Add the BCoV‑spiked DNA/RNA Shield to each conical so that the final concentration is ~75 mg dewatered solids per mL of shield; this ratio was chosen to avoid inhibition of SARS‑CoV‑2 digital PCR assays.

substeps.instruction: Add spiked shield to achieve ~75 mg solids / mL.

steps.title: Save spare spiked shield
steps.instruction: Save any remaining BCoV‑spiked DNA/RNA Shield for use as the extraction positive control template during RNA extraction.

steps.title: Add grinding balls
steps.instruction: Add 5–10 grinding balls to each conical tube.

steps.title: Secure tubes in Geno/Grinder
steps.instruction: Place the conicals in the adapters on the Geno/Grinder stage, tighten the clamp securely. (Instrument: SPEX Sample Prep Geno/Grinder, model 1006‑113806).

steps.title: Homogenize samples
steps.instruction: Run the Geno/Grinder for 2 minutes at 1 000 rpm to homogenize the samples.

steps.title: Pre‑heat oven and weigh boats
steps.instruction: Place aluminum weigh boats in the oven and pre‑heat to 110 °C.

substeps.instruction: Set oven to 110 °C and allow to pre‑heat.

steps.title: Record empty pan masses
steps.instruction: Weigh each empty aluminum pan and record its mass in grams.

steps.title: Add wet solids to pans
steps.instruction: Using a spatula, scoop a generous amount of dewatered solid into each pan.

steps.title: Record wet pan masses
steps.instruction: Weigh each pan containing wet solids and record the mass in grams.

steps.title: Dry solids overnight
steps.instruction: Place the pans in the oven inside the biosafety cabinet and leave to dry overnight.

steps.title: Measure dry mass and calculate percent
steps.instruction: After at least 6 hours (up to 24 hours) dry time, remove the pans, weigh them, and calculate dry‑weight percent using: 100 × [1 – (wet mass – dry mass) / wet mass].

substeps.instruction: Weigh dried pans and record mass.
Compute dry‑weight percent with the given formula.

steps.title: Dispose of dried pans
steps.instruction: Dispose of the aluminum pans in the red biohazard waste bin.

steps.title: Label storage conicals
steps.instruction: Apply a label for each sample to a 50 mL conical for storage.

steps.title: Store remaining solids and note conditions
steps.instruction: Pour up to 50 mL of the remaining primary settled solids into the labeled conical and store at 4 °C until quality‑control results are confirmed; dewatered solids may be stored at –80 °C. Note that up to 7 days at 4 °C has minimal effect on RNA targets, while freeze‑thaw cycles may affect quantification.

substeps.instruction: Transfer ≤50 mL remaining solids to labeled conical.

steps.title: Dispose of waste sludge and bottles
steps.instruction: Dispose of remaining sludge in a 4 L biohazard waste container prefilled with 400 mL bleach, then discard the sample bottles as biohazard waste.

substeps.instruction: Place sludge in 4 L container with 400 mL bleach.
Seal and dispose of container as biohazard waste.
Discard sample bottles in biohazard waste.
